newsitem.title: FINLAND: SAMPO SAYS ALLOWED TO TRANSFER INSURANCES.
newsitem.headline: SAMPO SAYS ALLOWED TO TRANSFER INSURANCES.

text.p: Finnish insurance group Vakuutusosakeyhtio Sampo said on Friday it had been allowed to transfer insurances from its Kaleva and Teollisuusvakuutus units to life insurance unit Henki-Sampo.

"The Ministry of Social Affairs and Health has allowed the transfer of the pension insurance portfolio of mutual insurance company Kaleva to Henki-Sampo and of life reinsurance policies from Teollisuusvakuutus Oy to Henki-Sampo," Sampo said in a statement.
The transfers would take place on January 1, 1997, it said.
The underwriting reserves transferred amount to about 2.6 billion markka in the pension insurance and about 270 million markka in life reinsurance, Sampo said.
The transfers are part of Sampo's reorganisation which aims to concentrate the unit-linked life insurance and pension insurance operations to Henki-Sampo, a Sampo spokesman said.

Henki-Sampo's share capital would also be boosted by up to 50 million markka to about 150 milliona and after the capital injection, Sampo would hold 50.5 percent of Henki-Sampo, Teollisuusvakuutus 30 percent and Kaleva 19.5 percent.
Henki-Sampo will start to sell new life insurance policies on January 1, 1997, Sampo said.
